processing: A strip-shaped green tea finished by baking (hongqing), which keeps a soft, clean aroma and leaves the fine down intact.
harvest_season: Around Qingming in early April, one bud with two leaves.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight, pointed strands, dark green and glossy, with plenty of down.
taste_profile: A clean, lasting fragrance over a mellow, full and refreshing cup.

brewing.notes: Two-leaf picking takes slightly hotter water than an all-bud tea. Keep the lid off between steeps.

vintage_note: As with other Mengshan greens, it is normally bought as the current spring's harvest and drunk within about a year. Lots from around Qingming are the ones the name refers to, so ask for the picking date.
description:
Mengshan Chunlu, spring dew of Mengshan, is a baked green tea from Mingshan on Mengding Mountain near Ya'an in Sichuan. It is a younger sibling in a famous family that also holds Mengding Ganlu, Shihua and Huangya.

The pick is a bud with two leaves around Qingming, a little more mature than the all-bud Mengding teas. Baking rather than pan-firing gives fine, pointed strands that stay dark green and downy.

Expect a steady, clean fragrance and a rounder, fuller body than the name might suggest, with a refreshing finish. Water around 85 C suits it; much hotter and the freshness goes first.

If you enjoy it, try a Mengding Ganlu beside it to taste what a more tender, curled style does on the same mountain.
history:
Mengshan Chunlu is a modern creation, developed in 1981 in Mingshan. It won a quality award from the Sichuan provincial agriculture department three years running, from 1983 to 1985.

It draws on the much older reputation of Mengshan tea, which local tradition traces to the Western Han and which was sent as tribute from the Tang onward. The tradition belongs to the mountain, not to this particular style.
